clue.text: Unacceptable to hold one idea

indicators.note: the first phrase is made to hold the second piece inside it

parts.note: something unacceptable is 'not on' in British idiom
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a single idea as unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British slang for unacceptable; holding I gives NOT-I-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, a straightforward synonym for an idea.

clue.text: Clear Navy's invading region ignoring Queen

indicators.note: the navy letter invades, going inside the shortened region word
ignoring the Queen means her letter is left out of the region word

parts.note: a district is an administrative region
R, for Regina, stands for the Queen
N is the abbreviation for Navy; the 's stands for 'is' linking to invading

explanation.surface: A naval force moves into territory, apparently disregarding the monarch's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring Queen' turns DISTRICT into DISTICT; 'invading' puts N inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and clear are synonyms describing something sharply defined and easy to perceive.

clue.text: Adjustment one time accommodated in redesign of one interior

indicators.note: the pair of letters is housed inside the rearranged letters
a redesign reworks the shape of the words that follow, signalling an anagram

parts.note: one can be the article A

explanation.surface: An interior designer reworks a room, adjusting one more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesign of' yields REORIENTION; 'accommodated in' slots the pair between its T and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A reorientation is a change of direction or attitude, a form of adjustment.

clue.text: Rectors and Dean excited about church turning up ready for use again?

indicators.note: the rearranged clergy go around the church letters
excited clergymen are stirred up, so their letters are rearranged
in a down clue the church letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Clergy get worked up about a church, perhaps one ready to reopen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' signals the anagram, 'turning up' the reversal and 'about' the wrap. The question mark flags a playful definition of a church blessed afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A church consecrated again is made fit once more for worship, hence ready for use again.

clue.text: I'm to continue retaining one — then I'm adopting second artistic style

parts.note: taken as written, I'M

indicators.note: the first stretch keeps the single letter inside it

parts.note: to press on is to continue
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the second I'm takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written, I'M

explanation.surface: A painter vows to press on, keeping going with a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts I into IM PRESS ON; 'adopting' puts S into IM, giving ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionism is the nineteenth-century French painting movement of Monet and Renoir, an art style.

clue.text: No indication of agreement? That is it

parts.note: saying OK shows agreement
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether silence means no agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a coy euphemism for sex, and so is the slang answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are playful euphemisms for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Lack of system in barristers sadly restricting opening of action

indicators.note: the anagram closes around the single letter, confining it
sadly suggests the words are in a sorry state, so their letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Barristers are lamented for their haphazard approach in getting a case going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges IN BARRISTERS; 'restricting' puts A, the opening of action, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrariness is decision by whim rather than principle, a lack of any system.

clue.text: Hesitation over volume accommodated by modern storage system is stressful

indicators.note: the word for modern takes the pair in, housing it

parts.note: modern means new

indicators.note: in a down clue the hesitation sits over, above, the volume letter

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
racking is shelving used to store things

explanation.surface: A warehouse worker finds a new shelving system nerve-shredding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down clue: the hesitation sits above the volume letter before 'accommodated by' houses both.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nerve-wracking causes anxiety and tension, which is what stressful means.

clue.text: Cut back on investing millions in share certificates

indicators.note: the money letter is invested, placed within the certificates word

parts.note: scrip is a term for share certificates
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: An investor economises by putting millions into shares.
explanation.walkthrough: Financial 'investing' disguises an insertion: M goes inside SCRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise or be sparing, to cut back spending.

clue.text: Military men, those penetrating satellites

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
biters are those whose teeth penetrate

explanation.surface: Soldiers breach enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbiters are bodies or spacecraft going round a planet, as satellites do.

clue.text: Bit of sound fed into various innocent ears making no objection

indicators.note: the single letter is fed inside the rearranged words
various suggests the letters take a different order
a bit of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Some noise is piped into unsuspecting ears, and nobody protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' signals the anagram and 'fed into' the insertion; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-resistance is passive acceptance, offering no objection or opposition.

clue.text: One's enveloped by kind spirit

indicators.note: the single letter is wrapped inside the word for kind

parts.note: a genus is a kind or class
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is', linking to enveloped

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by a benevolent spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enveloped by' puts I inside GENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius can be a guardian spirit or jinn, the old Roman sense.

clue.text: Carnal knowledge in it upset American shop-owner

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: R. H. Macy founded Macy's department store in New York

explanation.surface: A US store owner is embroiled in a sex scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IT into TI. Macy's is a famous New York department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimacy is a euphemism for a sexual relationship, matching carnal knowledge.

clue.text: Dressing right to be used amongst peeled potatoes

indicators.note: the letter is placed among the other letters, inside them
peeled means the outer skin, the first and last letters, is removed

parts.note: tatties is Scottish and northern British slang for potatoes

explanation.surface: A chef uses a dressing on peeled spuds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' turns TATTIES into ATTIE; R goes inside. 'Dressing' as salad dressing misleads; it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is clothing, what one dresses in, so dressing in the sense of garments.

clue.text: Energy required in one nursing job

indicators.note: the letter is needed inside the carer word

parts.note: a carer is one who looks after the sick
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Nursing takes a lot of energy as a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required in' puts E inside CARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a profession or occupation, so a job in the broad sense.

clue.text: Republican, intensely patriotic, expelling number on sound grounds?

indicators.note: expelling means a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: nationalistic means fervently devoted to one's nation

explanation.surface: A flag-waving Republican deports someone, claiming a solid reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelling' removes N from NATIONALISTIC. The question mark flags a cryptic definition: reasoned thinking stands on rational grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationalistic thinking bases belief on reason, so stands on logically sound grounds.

clue.text: Proposition is following article on sun

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the sun letter
the word is comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the is the definite article
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: An argument follows an article about the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the article above the sun letter in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward to be argued or proved.

clue.text: Revolutionary writer advancing power as poisonous stuff?

indicators.note: advancing means the letter moves forward to the front

parts.note: Tom Paine wrote Common Sense and Rights of Man in the American and French Revolutions

explanation.surface: A radical pamphleteer's growing power seems toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancing' moves P from the middle of TOMPAINE to the front. The question mark hedges: these compounds were once wrongly blamed for food poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are compounds formed in rotting protein, long blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Quote my words after returning purgative

indicators.note: returning means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to quote my words is to cite me

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be quoted after coming back from taking a laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads CITE ME backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic causes vomiting, a purge of the stomach, so a purgative in the broad sense.

clue.text: Sad about committee arranging experience for divers

indicators.note: the sad word goes around the committee letters

parts.note: depressing means making one sad

explanation.surface: A dispiriting meeting about a committee organising a diving trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' is only a link word here; divers ascending must ease pressure slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers surfacing slowly undergo decompression, letting pressure ease to avoid the bends.
